passage: At Zanele's birthday lunch in Toronto, Aunt Elif handed her a soft green parcel. Zanele tore the paper. Inside was a knitted sweater, and Zanele had hoped for paints. Her face fell for a moment. Papa touched her back. "Thank you, Aunt Elif," Zanele said. "I made it myself, one row a night," said Aunt Elif, beaming. That evening in her bedroom, Zanele whispered to Papa, "I wanted paints." "Thank you for saying thank you," he said. "Aunt worked hard on it. We can ask for paints another time."

qa.q: What gift did Aunt Elif give Zanele?
qa.a: She gave her a knitted green sweater that she had made herself.

qa.q: What was Zanele feeling when her face fell at the gift?
qa.a: She was disappointed because she had hoped for paints. She still said thank you, perhaps because Papa touched her back and Aunt Elif was so pleased.

qa.q: What did Papa do well when Zanele told him the truth?
qa.a: He let her be honest in private, thanked her for being kind at the party and said paints could be asked for another time. She did not have to hide her wish or hurt Aunt Elif. 🙂

qa.q: How does Aunt Elif see the moment when Zanele thanks her?
qa.a: She sees a happy niece and enjoys her one-row-a-night effort being noticed. She has no idea about the paints, so the thank you makes the gift feel worth the work.

grounding: A child says thank you for an unwanted gift, seeing the giver's effort, and honesty waits for a private moment.
